chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, and others, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from Abdullah ibn Maskan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Drinking as-sawiq with oil builds the flesh, strengthens the bone, softens the skin, and increases in sexual desire.

key_terms.السَّوِيق: A traditional food made from roasted flour, often mixed with water, oil, or honey.

ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of drinking sawiq with oil according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) underscores the Prophetic tradition of combining wheat flour with oil for optimal health, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical medicine (*al-tibb al-nabawi*). The narration details specific physiological benefits, including muscle growth, bone strengthening, skin softening, and enhanced libido, illustrating the holistic view of nutrition in Shia scholarship.
